home.heroTitle: From Dubai’s first school towards a university
home.heroBody: Al Ahmadiya School was founded in 1912 in Al Ras, Deira, by pearl merchant Sheikh Ahmed bin Dalmouk. More than a century later, it is preparing its next chapter as a proposed university.
home.heroCaption: The courtyard of the 1912 Al Ahmadiya School building — today a heritage museum managed by Dubai Culture.
home.welcomeTitle: A legacy of learning in Al Ras
home.welcomeBody1: Al Ahmadiya is regarded as Dubai’s first semi-formal school. Its classrooms around a courtyard taught the Qur’an, Arabic and arithmetic, and later the sciences, history and geography.
home.welcomeBody2: After educating more than 3,500 pupils, the school moved to a larger building in the early 1960s, and the original building was restored as a museum of education.

about.title: About Al Ahmadiya
about.subtitle: A school founded in 1912, preparing its next chapter
about.overview1: Al Ahmadiya School was established in 1912 in Al Ras, Deira, by Sheikh Ahmed bin Dalmouk, a leading pearl merchant. His son, Sheikh Mohammed bin Ahmed bin Dalmouk, completed the building and named the school in his father’s memory.
about.overview2: The school is remembered as Dubai’s first semi-formal school and one of the first regular schools when formal education was introduced in the emirate. Its original building was restored by the Government of Dubai and opened as a museum of education in 2000.
about.overview3: Al Ahmadiya is now preparing a transition towards a university. Details of the university will be published here as they are confirmed.
about.heritageBody: The two-storey building in Al Ras is arranged around an open courtyard, with carved arches, wooden-beamed galleries and a coral-stone base. It is today a heritage museum managed by Dubai Culture & Arts Authority, and is not part of the future university campus.
about.accreditationBody: The university’s licensing and accreditation status will be published here once granted by the relevant UAE authorities.
